rationale: The R&D-addback-to-liabilities conditioning on R&D intensity is internally consistent and the positive sign follows naturally from the expression, but the construct is close to a mechanical blend of two documented effects (R&D intensity premium and profitability/debt-coverage) and xrd/sale is unstable for low-sales firms, so incremental novelty is modest.

The loss indicator zeroes out the majority of firms, so the resulting spread mechanically goes long loss-making R&D firms and short *all* profitable firms — a bet against the profitability premium that the stated hypothesis never claims, on top of a severely degenerate mass-at-zero distribution.

The hypothesis, expression and negative sign line up cleanly and the R&D-acceleration × net-short-debt interaction is not a direct rediscovery, though the second leg is largely a repackaged cash/short-term-leverage distress measure and ACCEL of a ratio is noisy at annual frequency.

Economically coherent and correctly signed, but it is close to a straightforward "bad balance sheet is bad" composite of two familiar ingredients (goodwill intensity and working-capital deficiency) with limited genuinely cross-theme insight.

The negative-book-equity indicator restricts the informative long leg to a few percent of firms while assigning zero to everything else, guaranteeing sparse, unstable portfolio composition — exactly the coverage-driven artifact the objective warns against.

Signs and logic are consistent, but adding a flow (xrd) to a stock (intan) is dimensionally sloppy and the cash-burn-plus-leverage leg largely reproduces standard distress-risk underperformance, making this the most generic of the batch.
